findings.title: Plaintext passwords and PII are written to logs on signup
findings.explanation: The PR description says the logger already redacts sensitive fields. It doesn't. `src/lib/logger.ts` redacts only `authorization` and `token` (`REDACTED_KEYS`). `req.body` for signup contains `password` in plaintext, along with `email` and `organization`. Every signup attempt, including ones that fail validation, would write the user's raw password to stdout and so to the log aggregator, backups and anyone with log access. This also breaks the rule in `docs/CONVENTIONS.md:23`: 'Never log request bodies or headers on auth routes.' Remove this line. To debug failed validation, use `signupSchema.safeParse` and log only the field names and zod issue codes or paths, such as `result.error.issues.map(i => ({path: i.path, code: i.code}))`. You could also log the keys of the body and the types or lengths of values, never the values. Any logs already produced by a deployment of this change need to be purged, and affected passwords may need to be rotated.

findings.title: Redaction list is too narrow to rely on
findings.explanation: `REDACTED_KEYS` has only `authorization` and `token`. It misses `password`, `password_hash`, `secret`, `api_key`, `cookie` and similar. Even apart from this PR, the logger gives a false sense of safety. Consider extending the list, ideally with a denylist that includes `password`, so that future logging of bodies is less dangerous. This is defense in depth, not a substitute for removing the log line.

findings.title: Validation failures are not handled, so the debugging goal is better met here
findings.explanation: `signupSchema.parse` throws a ZodError on invalid input. Unless a global error handler maps it to a 400, this becomes a 500, and with Express 4 an async throw may not be caught at all. Using `safeParse`, returning a 400 with the issues, and logging a sanitized failure reason would solve the stated problem (not knowing why signups fail) without logging payloads.
